exposure: standard women (normal weight, nonsmoking, singleton primiparous women, 25-29 years old with no known comorbidity)
cohort: 31,386 singleton primiparous adolescents and 178,844 standard women
finding: The study found that obese adolescents had a higher risk for adverse obstetric outcomes compared to normal weight adolescents, while overweight adolescents had better outcomes compared to standard women.
